items.quote:
The tests are a headless harness, not the game client. Each spec `loadfile`s one production file
with stubbed host APIs: `model_spec` (Model.lua, Data/*.lua, Prices.lua), `prices_spec` (Prices.lua),

(UI hooks, menus, tooltips, the objective tracker, the trainer) is only verified in game. The
in-game check for data is `/su audit` with a profession open.

The Gate table's claim that every spec prints <name>_spec: N checks passed is contradicted by settings_spec.lua:114, which prints settings: ok. Describe actual coverage and retain in-game verification for rendering and real host integration.

# Opens a PR when wago.tools lists a newer Forever build whose recipe data differs, then runs CI

Correct both comments to explain the pending PR runs, and put the pack's approval step in the generated PR body beside its existing pre-merge instructions so maintainers do not mistake dispatched CI for completion of the PR checks.

items.quote: urgency[entry] = { #steps > 0 and 0 or 1, ns.IsTracked(skillLine) and 0 or 1, Urgency(entry) }
items.what: Stale cache: SkillUpForever.API.Professions() orders entries by ns.IsTracked (ns.db.trackedProfessions), but nothing invalidates the API cache when tracking changes. ns.SetTracked (Shopping.lua:230-234) only writes the DB and calls ns.RefreshTracker; it never calls ns.InvalidateAPI/ns.InvalidatePlans, and API.lua's event list has no tracking signal. So after the player tracks or untracks a profession on the route tab, Adventure Guide Forever keeps receiving the old order (the old tracked profession still first) until an unrelated event (bag update, zone change, skill change) happens. The header comment (API.lua:7, 'kept until skills, recipes, bags, prices or the zone change') also omits tracking as a dependency.
items.why: In-memory LuaJIT repro /tmp/api_track_repro.lua: tests/api_spec.lua's harness (Locales, Model, Route, Shopping, API loaded) with the real Shopping.lua ns.IsTracked/ns.SetTracked and db.trackedProfessions={[197]=true}. Output: 'before: Tailoring Blacksmithing'; after ns.SetTracked(197,false); ns.SetTracked(165,true): 'Tailoring Blacksmithing same table: true' (stale); after an unrelated BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED: 'Leatherworking Blacksmithing'. rg for InvalidateAPI/InvalidatePlans callers: Route.lua:131-133 (InvalidatePlans -> InvalidateAPI), Route.lua:751 (target commit), Trainer.lua:105, Core.lua:256, Prices.lua PricesChanged; none on the tracking path. Fix: call ns.InvalidateAPI() in ns.SetTracked (or have the API sort read tracking at call time), and add tracking to the header comment.
items.reason: same producer as c2721be8aa: ns.SetTracked in Shopping.lua never calls ns.InvalidateAPI

items.quote: local net = cost and cost - (value and value.copper or 0)
items.what: ns.Describe recomputes the net cost (reagent cost minus craft value) that ns.NetCost (Prices.lua:243-250) is the canonical home for; Route.lua:85/117/312/482 and Trainer.lua:64 use ns.NetCost, while row/tooltip text uses this copy. A change to what counts as net (e.g. valuing output differently) would have to land in both or rows and routes disagree.
items.why: Both copies today: cost = ns.RecipeCost(id); value = ns.CraftValue(id); net = cost - (value and value.copper or 0); identical, no stated reason for the divergence. Describe also needs `value` for its return, so the collapsed form is either `net = ns.NetCost(id)` (one extra CraftValue call) or NetCost returning (net, value) for Describe to reuse.
items.reason: Small idiom composed from the shared RoundMoney/FormatNet/RecipeCost helpers; Tooltip keeps copper precision and API formats only positive fees, so the variants serve different contracts

items.quote:
local bucket = source == "gather" and list.gather
				or source == "vendor" and list.vendor
				or source == "auctionator" and list.auction
				or list.unknown
items.what: The price-source set is still restated as bare literals and renamed on the way: Prices.lua:80/93/112 produce 'auctionator'|'gather'|'vendor' (alias SkillUpPriceSource, types/Namespace.lua:629); Model.ShoppingList (Model.lua:243-251) maps 'auctionator' to an 'auction' bucket and drops anything else into 'unknown'; the bucket set {gather, vendor, auction, unknown} is then restated at Model.lua:243, Shopping.lua:60 (iteration order), Route.lua:517 (SOURCE_TEXT), Shopping.lua:88, API.lua:95-102 and types/Namespace.lua:674; Route.lua:631 PriceAge and Tooltip.lua:125/134/160 compare the raw 'auctionator'. No constant table defines either set.
items.why: rg for '"auctionator"|"auction"|"gather"|"vendor"|"unknown"' across non-Data Lua shows the two spellings of one concept in 9 places. The profile's Anti-patterns name exactly this ('auctionator means auction' in Model.ShoppingList and Route.lua PriceAge) and it is unchanged. A new or renamed price source in Prices.lua falls silently into 'unknown' here (no error, unlike Tooltip.lua:163 which errors on an unknown source), and nothing but a manual search finds the other read sites. Canonical home: a single source-to-bucket table beside SkillUpPriceSource (Prices.lua or Core.lua), with ShoppingList erroring on an unmapped source.
items.reason: Price provenance (SkillUpPriceSource literal union) and acquisition buckets are distinct typed contracts; PriceAge reads Auctionator-specific age metadata, so 'auctionator' there is not the bucket

items.quote: local resale = mode == "auction" and auction and auction * (1 - AUCTION_CUT) or nil
items.what: Model.CraftValue treats any mode other than 'none' and 'auction' as 'vendor'. The mode is ns.db.craftValue (Prices.lua:228), a saved setting that Core.lua LoadDB only type-checks as a string (it validates reagentTooltip against its options, not craftValue), so an unknown saved value silently prices crafts at vendor sell price while types/Namespace.lua SkillUpDefaults claims craftValue is 'none'|'vendor'|'auction'.
items.why: Matches the profile's listed anti-pattern (saved setting read without checking against its options). Core.lua:70-87 LoadDB: `type(loaded[key]) ~= type(value)` for every key, then only reagentTooltip is checked against ns.REAGENT_TOOLTIP_OPTIONS. A stale/invalid craftValue string reaches Model.CraftValue and falls into the vendor branch (line 303), subtracting a vendor value from every recipe's cost with no signal. Fix belongs in LoadDB (validate craftValue, and sortMode, like reagentTooltip); Model's else-branch is where it surfaces.
items.reason: same producer as 20c0eeeaaa: Core.lua LoadDB accepts any string for craftValue and sortMode; one decision there settles it

items.quote: return cost - (value and value.copper or 0)
items.what: An unknown crafted-item sell value is silently treated as zero, yielding an apparently complete net cost and allowing routes to be ranked using incomplete price data.
items.why: SellPrice returns nil when the item cache and ItemSellPrices have no price, and CraftValue also returns nil for that case. NetCost conflates this with a known zero value, a non-item output, and the explicit craftValue="none" setting. An in-memory LuaJIT repro with known reagents costing 100 copper, a known item output of quantity 1, vendor valuation enabled, and no live or bundled sell price produced CraftValue=nil but NetCost=100. tools/README.md confirms that missing ItemSparse rows have no bundled value; the generator keeps only positive sell prices, so absent data does not establish a zero price. Route.lua RouteSnapshot and Trainable feed this numeric netCost into Model.PlanRoute, which excludes only nil costs. Core.lua Describe repeats the same zero substitution and exposes the result in row and tooltip cost-per-skill-up displays. Preserve unknown output value separately from disabled valuation and known zero/non-item output in both consumers.
items.reason: owner-delegated 2026-09-27: done, ledger refuses fixed because the anchored line legitimately stays: the subtraction remains but NetCost and Describe now return nil first when CraftValue flags an unknown sell price (model_spec).

items.quote:
local function Table(parent, key)
	if type(parent[key]) ~= "table" then
		parent[key] = {}
	end
	return parent[key]
end
items.what: Table(parent, key) generalizes a single vendor-table initialization in InitPrices; both parameters are fixed and its return value is discarded.
items.why: Whole-repository searches for Table and InitPrices across Lua, XML, TOC, Python, shell, workflows, docs and types found only the local definition and Table(ns.db, "vendor") in Prices.lua. The function is neither exported nor registered, and no second use or implementation exists in the tree. Replace the call with the same three-line type guard on ns.db.vendor inside InitPrices and remove the generic helper. This preserves initialization and existing persisted vendor data while removing two unnecessary parameters and an unused return; it does not remove the guard or change the saved schema.
items.guard: lens-only: spotting a single-caller helper whose arguments are always the same needs whole-file judgment

items.what: InitPrices re-validates ns.db.vendor, which LoadDB has already guaranteed is a table
items.why: Core.lua:407-408 runs LoadDB (its DEFAULTS loop at Core.lua:83-87 resets any non-table vendor to {}) immediately before InitPrices, and it is the only caller outside specs; prices_spec.lua:13 and model_spec always supply vendor = {}. The guard cannot fire.
items.reason: The guard supports model_spec's real partial-load initialization, where db.vendor has not been created by Core.LoadDB; removing it in memory causes Price to index nil at Prices.lua:98. The defensive-noise partial-load exception applies despite the full TOC path having validated the DB.

items.quote: local each = info.price / math.max(info.stackCount or 1, 1)
items.what: A merchant entry with a missing or zero stackCount is treated as a one-item stack, and the guessed unit price is persisted as an observed vendor price.
items.why: RecordMerchant checks that price is positive but never establishes the stack size. The pinned MerchantItemInfo declaration in .types/vscode-wow-api/Annotations/Core/Blizzard_APIDocumentationGenerated/MerchantFrameDocumentation.lua marks stackCount optional with default 0. An in-memory LuaJIT MERCHANT_SHOW repro using an item ID and price=100 recorded ns.db.vendor[itemID]=100 and returned Price(itemID).copper=100 with either absent stackCount or stackCount=0. That record takes precedence over ns.VendorPrices in Price and survives subsequent sessions, so unknown quantity becomes authoritative price data. Skip recording until a positive stack size is known, preserving any previously known unit price.
items.reason: owner-delegated 2026-09-27: merchant rows need a positive stackCount
items.guard: lens-only: prices_spec covers zero and missing stack sizes; a guessed divisor elsewhere needs judgment

items.what: unreachable branch: InitPrices re-defaults ns.db.vendor
items.why: Core.lua LoadDB runs immediately before ns.InitPrices (only caller) and its DEFAULTS loop already resets any non-table vendor to {}; prices_spec loads Prices.lua directly but sets its own ns.db. items.quote: return copper, okAge and type(days) == "number" and days or nil
items.what: A failed or missing GetAuctionAgeByItemID call gives days = nil, the same value as 'seen more than three weeks ago'
items.why: AuctionatorAPI() only checks GetAuctionPriceByItemID, so a build without the age function makes pcall fail. Tooltip.lua PriceAgeText then says 'over 3 weeks ago' and PriceAge counts 22 days, so Route.lua PriceAge shows every route in orange with 'rescan with Auctionator'. Unknown age should render as unknown, not as an invented 22 days.
items.reason: With a valid auction price but missing GetAuctionAgeByItemID, the unchanged price path returns days=nil; Tooltip.PriceAgeText then says over 3 weeks ago and PriceAge returns 1,900,800 seconds. The probe distinguishes missing capability from Auctionator's intentional old-age nil sentinel, so unknown age is incorrectly presented as known stale data.

items.quote: -- A day-old Auctionator price is flagged: auction prices move that fast.
items.what: stale: the comment says a day-old price is flagged
items.why: Auctionator reports whole days and PriceAge is days * 86400 (Tooltip.lua:128). The test is `ns.PriceAge(oldest) > STALE_AFTER` with STALE_AFTER = 86400, so days = 1 gives 86400 > 86400 = false and is not flagged. Flagging starts at 2 days, or when the age is unknown (22 days). Either the comment should say 'older than a day' (as 2+ days) or the comparison should be >=.
items.reason: Prices.PriceAge converts whole days to seconds and Render uses age > 86400, so an exactly one-day-old price is not flagged although the comment says day-old. This is an inaccurate explanatory boundary, not an ordering or threshold change to make in this audit.
items.guard: lens-only: deciding whether a comment describes the strict threshold correctly requires the integer-day producer and UI wording contracts

items.quote:
while rank and segment.toSkill - profession.modifier > rank.cap - 75 do
			steps[#steps + 1] = { rank = rank }
items.what: Bug: a segment crossing a skill cap can place rank training before the player meets its required skill.
items.why:
RouteSteps tests the segment endpoint and inserts the rank before the whole segment, without checking its starting skill against rank.reqSkill or splitting the segment. With bundled Heavy Linen Bandage thresholds, First Aid 40/75 targeting 90 produces 'Train Journeyman at 50' followed by one craft segment from 40 to 90. The first action is impossible at 40. RenderRoute and API.lua Steps consume this order directly; RequiresLine also assumes the route has reached the prerequisite before training. The ordered route needs a craft segment reaching the training point before this rank, followed by the remaining crafts. Executed an in-memory LuaJIT reproduction from the repository root (no files written):
luajit - <<'LUA'
local ns = {db={trainer={},routeTargets={}}, InvalidateAPI=function() end}
local known, costs = {}, {}
ns.IsLearned=function(id) return known[id] == true end
ns.NetCost=function(id) return costs[id] end
local env=setmetatable({APPRENTICE='Apprentice', JOURNEYMAN='Journeyman', EXPERT='Expert', ARTISAN='Artisan'}, {__index=_G})
for _,file in ipairs({'Locales/enUS.lua','Data/Thresholds.lua','Data/Recipes.lua','Data/Trainer.lua','Model.lua','Route.lua'}) do
  setfenv(assert(loadfile(file)),env)('SkillUpForever',ns)
end
known[3275], costs[3275], known[3276], costs[3276] = true, 1, true, 1
ns.db.routeTargets[129]=90
local p={skillLine=129,name='First Aid',skill=40,base=40,max=75,modifier=0,capped=false}
local r=ns.PlanRoute(p)
local s=ns.RouteSteps(p,r)
assert(s[1].rank.reqSkill==50 and s[1].rank.reqSkill>p.base)
assert(s[2].segment.recipeID==3276 and s[2].segment.fromSkill==40 and s[2].segment.toSkill==90)
print(s[1].rank.name,s[1].rank.reqSkill,s[2].segment.fromSkill,s[2].segment.toSkill) -- Journeyman 50 40 90
LUA
items.reason: Fixed at the producer: ns.PlanRoute now splits a segment that crosses a rank's cap from below its reqSkill (SplitAtRank), so these RouteSteps lines, still correct, place the rank between the halves (route_spec 'crafts up to the skill Journeyman needs'). The quote stays, so the ledger cannot record fixed; re-anchor on the next audit

items.quote:
if #route.segments == 0 and route.excluded.unpriced > 0 then
		-- Auctionator knows only what it has scanned, so installing it isn't enough.
items.what: Bug: an unpriced, already-grey recipe hides valid continuation suggestions and gives an irrelevant pricing explanation.
items.why:
Model.PlanRoute counts every unpriced known recipe, including recipes already grey at the current skill. RenderRoute treats any positive count as proof that prices caused the blockage; its elseif then prevents RenderSuggestions. A real-data repro at Tailoring 100/150, target 125, with known unpriced recipe 2393 has six eligible scroll suggestions from Sources.lua, but RenderRoute never asks for them and shows only the Auctionator message. Pricing that grey recipe cannot let it skill up. Filter pricing blockers to recipes that could still help, and allow no_recipe suggestions even when pricing information is also shown. The repro obtains private render functions through debug.getupvalue in the headless LuaJIT harness; it does not create or operate client frames. Executed an in-memory LuaJIT reproduction from the repository root (no files written):
luajit - <<'LUA'
local ns = {db={trainer={},routeTargets={}}, InvalidateAPI=function() end}
local known, costs = {}, {}
ns.IsLearned=function(id) return known[id] == true end
ns.NetCost=function(id) return costs[id] end
local env=setmetatable({APPRENTICE='Apprentice', JOURNEYMAN='Journeyman', EXPERT='Expert', ARTISAN='Artisan'}, {__index=_G})
for _,file in ipairs({'Locales/enUS.lua','Data/Thresholds.lua','Data/Recipes.lua','Data/Trainer.lua','Model.lua','Route.lua'}) do
  setfenv(assert(loadfile(file)),env)('SkillUpForever',ns)
end
env.UnitFactionGroup=function() return 'Alliance' end
env.UnitPosition=function() end
env.tContains=function(t,v) for _,x in ipairs(t) do if x==v then return true end end return false end
for _,file in ipairs({'Data/Sources.lua','Sources.lua'}) do setfenv(assert(loadfile(file)),env)('SkillUpForever',ns) end
ns.HasAuctionator=function() return false end
known[2393]=true
ns.db.routeTargets[197]=125
local p={skillLine=197,name='Tailoring',skill=100,base=100,max=150,modifier=0,capped=false}
local r=ns.PlanRoute(p)
assert(#r.segments==0 and r.excluded.unpriced==1 and ns.Model.Color(ns.Model.Get(2393),p.skill)=='grey')
assert(#ns.RecipeSuggestions(p,r.reachedSkill)==6)
local called,original=0,ns.RecipeSuggestions
ns.RecipeSuggestions=function(...) called=called+1; return original(...) end
local function up(fn,want)
  for i=1,100 do local n,v=debug.getupvalue(fn,i); if not n then break end; if n==want then return v end end
  error('missing upvalue '..want)
end
local render=up(up(ns.RefreshRoute,'Render'),'RenderRoute')
render({Message=function(_,msg) print(msg) end,Add=function() error('unexpected row') end},p,r)
assert(called==0)
-- Prints only: These reagents have no vendor price. Auction prices need Auctionator.
LUA
items.reason: Model.PlanRoute counts only unpriced recipes that still skill up, so a grey one no longer blocks the suggestions
items.guard: lens-only: a behaviour bug, not a shape a rule can match; regression test tests/model_spec.lua 'a grey unpriced recipe keeps nothing out of the route'

items.quote: return C_Spell.GetSpellName(recipeID) or string.format(L["recipe %d"], recipeID)

items.quote: if price and price.source == "auctionator" and (not oldest or ns.PriceAge(price) > ns.PriceAge(oldest)) then
items.what: PriceAge re-fetches ns.Price for each reagent and re-decides 'is this an auction price' by the literal "auctionator", although each SkillUpNeededItem already carries the bucketed source ("auction"). Two vocabularies for one concept: price sources 'vendor'|'auctionator'|'gather' (compared by literal in Tooltip.lua:125/134/160, Model.lua:250, Route.lua:535/631, API.lua:114/133) and reagent buckets 'gather'|'vendor'|'auction'|'unknown'; the "auctionator means auction" mapping is restated here and in Model.ShoppingList.
items.why: Profile Anti-patterns names exactly this shape. SkillUpPriceSource is an alias (types/Namespace.lua:234) but LuaLS does not check equality comparisons against it, so a typo or a new source (e.g. a second AH addon) silently yields no price-age line. The guard is needed only because ns.PriceAge (Tooltip.lua:124) errors on non-auctionator prices; filtering on item.source == "auction" would read the already-computed bucket instead of restating the mapping.
items.reason: Price provenance (SkillUpPriceSource literal union) and acquisition buckets are distinct typed contracts; PriceAge reads Auctionator-specific age metadata, so 'auctionator' there is not the bucket

Proposed split: planning (1) into its own TOC file (e.g. Plan.lua) before Route.lua, leaving Route.lua as the page UI (2-5); a planning change would then not touch the UI file. Not performed.

TOC ordering permits that separation but does not force it now; the earlier owner deferral is preserved as context, not a refutation. Owner question: When Route.lua is next substantially changed, split its planning API from page rendering and profession-window wiring in a separately reviewed change?

items.quote:
if target > rank.cap - 75 then
			route.ranks[#route.ranks + 1] = rank
			route.trainingCost = route.trainingCost + rank.fee
items.what: Bug: incomplete plans charge rank-training fees for skill caps the route never reaches.
items.why:
PlanRoute uses the requested target to append ranks after Model.PlanWithTraining has already established the actual reachedSkill. With bundled Linen Bandage data, First Aid 1/75 targeting 100 can stop at 60 while still adding the 500-copper Journeyman fee. RouteSteps emits no rank step because no segment crosses 75, but RenderRoute adds trainingCost to the displayed total, and Shopping.lua TrainingSteps advertises the unused rank. Whole-repository searches for TrainerRanks, rank.fee, PlanRoute and RouteSteps found no subsequent pruning. Compare the reached base skill, accounting for profession.modifier, when selecting required ranks. Executed an in-memory LuaJIT reproduction from the repository root (no files written):
luajit - <<'LUA'
local ns = {db={trainer={},routeTargets={}}, InvalidateAPI=function() end}
local known, costs = {}, {}
ns.IsLearned=function(id) return known[id] == true end
ns.NetCost=function(id) return costs[id] end
local env=setmetatable({APPRENTICE='Apprentice', JOURNEYMAN='Journeyman', EXPERT='Expert', ARTISAN='Artisan'}, {__index=_G})
for _,file in ipairs({'Locales/enUS.lua','Data/Thresholds.lua','Data/Recipes.lua','Data/Trainer.lua','Model.lua','Route.lua'}) do
  setfenv(assert(loadfile(file)),env)('SkillUpForever',ns)
end
known[3275], costs[3275] = true, 1
ns.db.routeTargets[129]=100
local p={skillLine=129,name='First Aid',skill=1,base=1,max=75,modifier=0,capped=false}
local r=ns.PlanRoute(p)
local shown=0
for _,s in ipairs(ns.RouteSteps(p,r)) do if s.rank then shown=shown+1 end end
assert(r.reachedSkill==60 and r.stopReason=='no_recipe')
assert(r.trainingCost==500 and #r.ranks==1 and shown==0)
print(r.reachedSkill,r.trainingCost,#r.ranks,shown) -- 60 500 1 0
LUA
items.reason: PlanRoute picks ranks from route.reachedSkill, not the target
items.guard: lens-only: a behaviour bug, not a shape a rule can match; regression test tests/route_spec.lua 'a rank past where the route stops is not trained'

{ "none", L["Don't count it"] },
			{ "vendor", L["Vendor sell price"] },
			{ "auction", L["Auction price if higher"] },
items.what: The craftValue option set {'none','vendor','auction'} is spelled inline here while its siblings live in named tables (ns.SORT_OPTIONS, ns.REAGENT_TOOLTIP_OPTIONS in Core.lua:29-39). The same set is restated in Core.lua:11 (comment), Model.lua:291 (param annotation) and types/Namespace.lua:502, and compared by literal in Model.CraftValue (Model.lua:295, 299).
items.why: Because the set has no table, Core.lua LoadDB (lines 83-90) can only validate reagentTooltip against ns.REAGENT_TOOLTIP_OPTIONS; a stale or mistyped saved craftValue (e.g. an old 'auctionator') passes the type check at Core.lua:79 and Model.CraftValue silently treats it as 'vendor' (mode ~= 'auction' and ~= 'none'). Hoisting it to ns.CRAFT_VALUE_OPTIONS next to the other two option tables lets Settings and LoadDB share one definition. (The same gap exists for sortMode: RecipeList.lua:137 SORT_KEYS[ns.db.sortMode] with no LoadDB check; that is the profile's silent-fallbacks anti-pattern, outside this batch's lenses.)
items.reason: same producer as 20c0eeeaaa: Core.lua LoadDB accepts any string for craftValue and sortMode; one decision there settles it
